newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI raises export credit target to 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: India RBI raises export credit target to 12 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Saturday it has decided to raise banks' export credit target to 12.0 percent from 10.0 percent.
This was being done "recognising the paramount need to promote exports" and recent fall in export credit, the RBI said, announcing its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
It said export credit had fallen by 44.64 billion rupees, or 14.1 percent, to 272.94 billion between April 1 and September 27 this year.
Banks must attain the revised target by end-March 1997, the RBI said.
"Failure to achieve the stipulated level of export credit target could invite bank-specific policy responses," the central bank (RBI) said.
